How to measure it: switch the motor off, ride uphill at a steady pace for 5 to 10 minutes and record the ride. Afterwards the Avinox app lists the value in the ride data as the rider’s power.

Torque set 15 Nm below the next mode so the strong modes stay distinct.
The watt limit is fully available at your cadence.
Not adjustable, for 60 seconds at most. Full %1$s W from %2$s rpm.
Avinox %1$s setup (%2$s kg total, %3$s rpm, %4$s W rider power)
%1$s: assist level %2$s · max. %3$s W · max. %4$s Nm
Max. watts = target in watts per kg of total weight × %1$s kg, rounded to 50 W and capped at what the motor and the mode allow.
Max. Nm = max. watts ÷ %1$s rpm × 9.55, rounded up to a full 5 Nm. That makes the watt limit available at your cadence.
Assist level = max. watts ÷ %1$s W rider power. The next higher level that delivers this assistance is chosen.
AUTO and TRAIL get a range: the upper value from the calculation, the lower one follows on from the mode below.
With “All modes”, the range modes (%1$s) deliberately keep the assist level below the watt limit. The strongest mode uses the motor’s maximum and gets one level in reserve.
Create the modes marked “create” as additional modes in the Avinox Ride app, with name and colour, and arrange them in this order.
On the flat, switch to one of the three lowest modes. That gives the most range.
In the strong modes, approach the overrun setting (how long the motor keeps pushing after you stop pedalling) from a medium value. With a long overrun the bike keeps pushing in tight uphill corners.
Set the mode order in the app to ECO, AUTO, TRAIL, TURBO. Then you shift from weak to strong.
With real-time tuning you change the assist level from the handlebar while riding.
Choose your battery. On the M2S it sets the peak power in Boost: 1,500 W with FP700 or RS800, 1,300 W with FS800 or FS600.
With this battery the M2S delivers up to %1$s W in Boost.
